html:
The Confederation of the Rhine was a league of German states set up by Napoleon in July 1806, with himself as its "protector". It lasted until his defeat in 1813.

Sixteen states signed first, and left the Holy Roman Empire. A few weeks later the emperor Francis II gave up the old imperial crown, and the Empire ended after about a thousand years. In the next years nearly every German state joined, except Austria and Prussia, until the league had about three dozen members.

Napoleon rewarded his allies with land taken from church states, free cities and small lordships, and with higher titles:

  • Bavaria and Württemberg became kingdoms in 1806, and Saxony later that year.
  • Baden and Hesse-Darmstadt became grand duchies.
  • Smaller members such as Nassau grew by swallowing their neighbours.

In return they had to send troops to Napoleon's wars, including tens of thousands to the invasion of Russia in 1812. Many members brought in French-style reforms. After the defeat at Leipzig in 1813 the league broke up as its rulers switched sides. The Congress of Vienna replaced it with the German Confederation, but the simpler map of fewer, larger states stayed.
sum: The Confederation of the Rhine was a league of German states set up by Napoleon in July 1806, with himself as its "protector". It lasted until his defeat in 1813.
